design_rationale:
WHY A GOOD TEST. A pickup owner five weeks into new tires wants to return them under the satisfaction guarantee for his money back. The scored figure is the trial refund on the set's ticket T-16034418 (872.70, to the bank card). On October 12 the Fairlawn store found a shifted belt in the right front tire (inspection c52f4f0f, defect belt_shift), replaced it on the spot under the workmanship warranty and took the customer's share at the counter on his Crestline credit card (card purchase of 2026-10-12 at Fairlawn, ticket T-16188204, 3.53 = share 3.31 plus the point-of-sale tax line), but the warranty posting of that replacement to the tire set is missing. The trial refund is figured from the set's warranty ledger: the line's rule refunds the installation part only where a workmanship entry exists, and the share paid for the replaced tire is refunded from the share recorded on that entry, on its own counter ticket T-16188204 to the Crestline card that paid it (base tires_refund_tender: each ticket back to its own tender, never split, never to another tender). The agent must (1) find the trial-refund prerequisite sentence "The trial refund is not paid until every manufacturing defect recorded on an inspection entry of the set carries a workmanship replacement entry on the set." and see the RF defect without an entry, (2) compute and post the workmanship share (five factors over trial timing, defect class, rotation history, alignment plan and road hazard certificate), (3) compute the refund (four factors) and hand the confirmation to the customer. No paper record of work that never happened: the replacement was physically made at the store; only the posting is missing.

SCOPE. Draw: prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[5,4]: workmanship share 5, trial refund 4. Task 1 claims tires_ext_workmanship_share and tires_ext_trial_refund and their tools record_workmanship_replacement_cc1528ea (agent) and confirm_trial_return_33503dcd (user). Task 0 holds the adjustment, share settlement, ticket balance and lapsed-order refund; the two scopes are disjoint and every extended policy is claimed once.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root tires_ext_trial_refund (user tool confirm_trial_return_33503dcd, scored arg amount). One edge -> tires_ext_workmanship_share, value_input, gate install_part, state form, prerequisite sentence above. False at opening: inspection c52f4f0f (RF, 2026-10-12, 35480 mi) records belt_shift and set D (dd495945) has no tires_workmanship_replacement entry. Only the workmanship posting books such an entry. Order: posting (step 14) then confirmation (step 16). Deletion sensitivity (executed): replayed without the posting, the refund on the set's ticket is 756.70 instead of 872.70 (installation part back to the line rule, 0.00 on this line) and there is no workmanship entry to refund the 3.31 share from and leaves the RF entry missing from the terminal state. user_scenario asks only for the return; the October 12 visit is described only if the agent asks. Tool bodies create unconditionally.

FACTOR CARD. tires_ext_workmanship_share = 3.31 (all baselines 86.00): proration_basis_method mileage share inside the trial (2360 x 100 / 65000 = 3.6308%) -> 22.80; defect_class_cut 40% of the prorated share off (belt shift) -> 6.62; maintained_set_discount 10% of it off (1 rotation >= 2360 // 5000) -> 4.14; alignment_maintained_discount 10% of it off (3-Year plan, alignment 2026-09-09; alignment cross-difficulty) -> 4.14; replacement_mounting_waiver 0 (active Road Hazard Plus 36-Month certificate includes mounting; hazard cross-difficulty, multi-source with the set's line) -> 32.31. Arithmetic: not free (tread worn 14 - 11 = 3 > 2); each cut a percentage of the prorated share, worked out on its own: 3.6308 x (100 - 40 - 10 - 10)% = 1.4523%; 228.00 x 1.4523% = 3.31; mounting 0.
tires_ext_trial_refund = 872.70 (all baselines 862.00): refunded_installation_part 116.00 (workmanship entry on the set -> 4 x 29.00) -> 756.70; trial_usage_charge per-mile (2360 > 2000 and 35 days > 22.5 -> 2360 x 0.005 x 4 = 47.20) -> 919.90; alignment_bundle_recapture 15.00 (plan bought 2026-09-09, same day as install, at 189.99 below plan price 219.99, one alignment) -> 887.70; truck_size_restock 43.10 (LT line kept 35 days, 5% of 862.00) -> 915.80. Arithmetic: 4 x 228.00 - 50.00 = 862.00 + 116.00 - 47.20 - 15.00 - 43.10 = 872.70 to the bank card; separately 3.31 on T-16188204 to the Crestline card.

PAIRWISE METHOD TIERS (forced in this world, tiers.py): proration mileage 3.31 / time 1.52 / tread 22.80; usage per_mile 872.70 / flat 895.90 / none 919.90. All pairwise distinct.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Posting: set_active_workmanship (set D active); workmanship_within_term (2026-09-08 + 60 months = 2031-09-08, inclusive). Return: set_active_trial; within_trial_period (install 2026-09-09 + 45 days = 2026-10-24, inclusive; 2026-10-14 inside; 2026-10-25 outside); refund dedup (only refund on file a122577b, ticket T-13317725 on the Civic set, so none for T-16034418).

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Refund object: set D, ticket T-16034418, tender bank_card. Workmanship object: inspection c52f4f0f (RF); the posting cites it, carries the Fairlawn store 1452 and event date 2026-10-12. Excluded: Civic set 1e25e47b with its 2023 return request and refund (476.00), the alignment ticket T-16034420, LF/LR/RR inspections (13/32, no defect).

WORLD ROWS. Customer; Ram 1500 + Civic; set D + rotation 2026-10-05 (maintained discount) + 4 inspections 2026-10-12 (defect, odometer for usage and proration, tread worn); Civic set + return request + refund (dedup near-miss, decoy refund); Road Hazard Plus certificate + roadside allowance row (mounting waiver); 3-Year Alignment Plan + purchase alignment (alignment discount, bundle recapture); Fairlawn store (posting store); Crestline card account (active, ending 1846, balance 3.53) + its one card purchase of 2026-10-12 at Fairlawn, ticket T-16188204, 3.53 (the record of the counter payment for the replaced RF tire; the tires charter posts a ticket paid with the Crestline card to the card account, and sales tax is a separate point-of-sale line never part of a charter computation, so 3.53 = 3.31 share + 0.22 tax at 6.75%).

EDGE PROBES (probe.py): WRK defect inspection copied onto the Civic set -> 3.31 (unchanged, holding-scoped); WRK alignment plan removed -> 3.73; WRK hazard certificate removed -> 32.31; SAT Civic refund removed -> 872.70 (unchanged); SAT plan purchase moved to 2026-10-20 -> 887.70 (no recapture); SAT plan removed -> 887.70; SAT card account and card purchase removed -> 872.70 (the set's refund does not read them; only the share's ticket and tender come from them); SAT set D charged to a fleet account with a 43.10 tires-invoice discount -> 831.75.

PERSONA. Ignatius Ferreira-Holm, structural engineer, dry and precise; volunteers the return request and phone 3305550173; ZIP 44313, email, date of birth, odometer 35612, tender, refund choice, the October 12 swap and his counter payment on the Crestline card, and the Civic history only when asked; accepts store-side recording; confirms the hand-over as given; closes on confirmation.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate and verify (phone + ZIP); read sets, tire history, return requests, vehicles, stores, hazard certificates and events, alignment plan and events, card account and card transactions (the 2026-10-12 counter payment confirms the store swap). Post the RF workmanship replacement (set D, source c52f4f0f, store 1452 Fairlawn, RF, belt_shift, 3.31). Hand over the trial return (satisfaction_refund, 35612, T-16034418, satisfaction_trial_return, 872.70; share ticket T-16188204, crestline_card, 3.31).

MOST LIKELY ERRORS. Confirming the return without posting (756.70); using the tread share 22.80 instead of the in-trial mileage share; charging the line mounting 29.00 despite the certificate waiver; a flat usage fee instead of per-mile; missing the bundled-plan recapture; using the reported 35612 odometer instead of the inspection reading for usage.

VERIFICATION. Harness + real-tool replay reproduce 3.31 and 872.70 equal to computations and gold; per-task gates check_extended, check_solvability, replay_tasks, check_compute, check_grounding --task 1 OK.

REVISIONS (round 2). F-CHAIN-WRK: the workmanship replacement is a store-performed, customer-paid replacement whose posting is missing; the prerequisite is a real back-office precondition because the trial refund returns the paid share. No card factor; the alignment plan was paid by bank card. WRK tiers timed at the replacement visit; defect selection priority stated in the rule; tool takes store_id and dates the entry at the source inspection.

REVISIONS (round 3). O-T1-EVIDENCE: the store swap and counter payment are now on record: the share was paid with the Crestline card, so the card purchase row of 2026-10-12 at Fairlawn (ticket T-16188204, 3.53 incl. tax) sits next to inspection c52f4f0f; two card reads added before the posting (gold steps 11-12), the posting and confirmation moved to steps 14 and 16; persona says he paid with his Crestline credit card. Figures at round 3: 3.31, 876.01 (superseded in round 4). Shared charter edits re-verified on this task: the trial refund's tire price paid now also takes off the fleet discount of a fleet-charged ticket (set D is bank_card, no fleet invoice: 862.00 unchanged); F-MOUNT-HALF edit is in the share settlement only.

REVISIONS (round 4). F-TENDER: the share paid on the Crestline card under its own counter ticket is no longer added to the bank-card refund. The trial refund on the set's ticket is the tire price paid plus the installation part less usage, recapture and restock (872.70 to the bank card); the same confirmation books a second refund entry on T-16188204 for the 3.31 recorded on the workmanship entry, to crestline_card; the tool books only the tire refund entries, and the card account's merchandise credit is posted by the tires_refund event's card trigger (card:card_merchandise_credit when payment_method is crestline_card), not by the tool. Base tires_refund_tender holds for both tickets. The edge still bears weight: replayed without the posting the set's refund is 756.70 and no share entry exists to refund. Prerequisite gate moved from wrk_shares to install_part; all-baseline 862.00; sensitivities 756.70 / 919.90 / 887.70 / 915.80. O-FLEET-DISC: the rule now states the whole tires-invoice discount is counted against the tire price, the part taken on the mounting and kit lines included, in the four policies that use the clause. Sales tax: the 0.22 tax line of the 3.53 card purchase is returned by the point-of-sale tax line, never part of the policy figures (tires charter).

REVISIONS (round 5, render-source notes). The workmanship share no longer chains its factors: the defect class, the maintained-set discount and the alignment-maintained discount each take their own percentage of the prorated share off (structural defect 40%, bead leak 25%), assembled once in the share percentage; the ordering sentence is gone. Gold unchanged (3.31, 872.70, share refund 3.31; skip-posting replay 756.70); sensitivities 22.80 / 6.62 / 4.14 / 4.14 / 32.31. The rule now states that a set with no defect entry has no share (0.00), and that the trial refund's miles run are 0 for a set with no tread inspection entry. The trial-refund confirmation overwrite and amount overwrite restate the base clause for every return outside this policy before naming its own scope. Tool docstring: the call books only tire refund entries; the card merchandise credit is posted by the refund event's trigger. Probes: belt shift turned into a bead leak -> share 4.55; defect row cleared -> 0.00; no inspection entries -> trial refund 919.90.

REVISIONS (round 7, KB audit S2/KB-E3). The workmanship share's baseline no longer defines the miles run, which the baseline formula never uses; the miles run (that entry's odometer minus install_odometer) is stated inside the proration and maintained-set tiers, each factor with its own binding. The trial refund's days kept and miles run are stated inside the installation-part, usage and truck-restock tiers instead of a general sentence. No figure moved (3.31, 872.70, share refund 3.31; sensitivities unchanged). Probes: 3 extra rotations -> 3.31; installed 2026-09-25 (19 days kept) -> 936.76.
user_scenario:
You are Ignatius Ferreira-Holm, a structural engineer from Fairlawn, Ohio, calling Crestline customer care on your lunch break. You are polite, precise and a bit dry, you speak in short sentences, and you want a clear answer rather than a sales pitch.
On September 8 you bought a set of four Crestline Highway Terrain LT 65K tires for your 2020 Ram 1500 at the Fairlawn store, and they were mounted the next day. You have not been happy with them: there is a hum on the highway and a shimmy around 60 mph that a balance did not cure. You remember the salesman saying there was a satisfaction guarantee on new tires, and you want to return the set and get your money back rather than try another line. You open with that, in your own words, and you give your phone number, 3305550173, so they can find you. You know nothing about how a refund is worked out and you do not know any amount.
Other details you give only when the agent asks: your billing ZIP code is 44313; your email is ignatius.fholm@lakeviewmail.net; your date of birth is November 19, 1984. If asked for the odometer, the dash read 35612 this morning. If asked how you paid for the tires, you paid with your bank card. If asked whether you want money back or a different tire, you want the money back. If asked about the store visit on October 12, you say the technician found something wrong inside the right front tire, the store swapped it for a new one on the spot, and you paid your part of the new tire at the counter with your Crestline credit card; the shimmy is still there. You also have a 2017 Honda Civic; if the agent asks, you say you once returned a set of tires on the Civic under the guarantee, back in 2023. You do not raise anything else.
If the agent tells you something has to be recorded or taken care of on Crestline's side first, you say that is fine and let them do it. When the agent hands you the return to confirm yourself, you confirm it with exactly the details the agent gives you and read back what it shows if asked. You do not propose figures or steps and you do not haggle. Once the agent tells you the return is confirmed and the refunds are on their way, you thank them and hang up; you ask for nothing else.
